Update:

I narrowed the issue down further.

VRChat OSC freezes/crashes when AdGuard for Windows is enabled, and OSC works normally when AdGuard is disabled.

AdGuard version:

AdGuard 7.22.8 (5279)

AdGuard Network setting:

Filtering driver: SockFilter (experimental)

I also tested the following separately:

* SteamVR

* SteamVR add-ons / overlay apps

* Virtual Desktop

* VR-related add-ons

* VPN-related software

These do not appear to be the root cause by themselves.

This looks related to AdGuard's system-level traffic filtering interacting with VRChat OSC initialization.

After the failed initialization, VRChat can still remain stuck on the next launch because the OSC enabled PlayerPrefs value remains saved:

HKCU\Software\VRChat\vrchat

UI.Settings.Osc_h1043380067 = 1

Resetting this value back to 0 still recovers the client:

REG ADD HKCU\Software\VRChat\vrchat /v "UI.Settings.Osc_h1043380067" /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

Current workaround:

Disable AdGuard for Windows before enabling/using OSC. I will also test whether excluding VRChat.exe from AdGuard filtering is enough.

details:
VRChat becomes unresponsive immediately after I enable OSC.

Build:

VRChat 2026.2.2p2-1855-4c1f48c1eb-Release

Store:

Steam

Platform:

Windows standalone

Mode:

Desktop / --no-vr

System:

OS: Windows 11 64-bit

CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D

GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti

RAM: 64 GB

Steps to reproduce:

1. Make sure OSC is disabled / reset the OSC PlayerPrefs value to 0.

2. Launch VRChat from Steam in desktop mode with --no-vr.

3. Log in and enter a world.

4. Open Settings and enable OSC.

5. VRChat freezes / becomes unresponsive.

6. After force-closing the client, VRChat may continue freezing on launch until the OSC PlayerPrefs registry value is reset.

Observed result:

After enabling OSC, this PlayerPrefs value changes from 0 to 1:

HKCU\Software\VRChat\vrchat

UI.Settings.Osc_h1043380067

Normal / recoverable state:

UI.Settings.Osc_h1043380067 = 0

Broken state:

UI.Settings.Osc_h1043380067 = 1

Resetting only this value back to 0 allows VRChat to launch again:

REG ADD HKCU\Software\VRChat\vrchat /v "UI.Settings.Osc_h1043380067" /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

Expected result:

Enabling OSC should not freeze the client. If OSC initialization fails, VRChat should remain responsive and should not get stuck in a broken launch state.

Additional testing:

* I already tried common troubleshooting such as driver updates, reinstall/removal steps, and registry reset.

* No process appeared to be using UDP 9000 or 9001 before launch.

* There was no existing OSC folder/config to clear.

* I tested a separate local VRChat profile and different OSC ports using:

--profile=1 --osc=9010:127.0.0.1:9011

The launch options were applied, but enabling OSC still froze the client.

* I also tested on a separate Windows user account with a fresh HKCU/AppData user profile, and the same freeze still occurred when enabling OSC.

* I also tested with FlooCast/FMA120/Bluetooth disabled, but the issue still occurred.

Windows Error Reporting also generated an APPCRASH report after the OSC freeze/crash:

EventType: APPCRASH

Application: VRChat.exe

Faulting module: GameAssembly.dll

Exception code: c0000005

Exception offset: 0000000006736517

I also attempted to capture a dump:

* Task Manager produced a 0-byte dump.

* ProcDump full dump (-ma) failed with: Target process no longer running / 0x800707D1.

* ProcDump mini dump (-mm) failed with the same error.

Attached:

1. Redacted output_log

2. Minimal registry diff showing the OSC PlayerPrefs value change

3. Short reproduction video
title: Enabling OSC freezes VRChat; PlayerPrefs UI.Settings.Osc_h1043380067 set to 1 causes client hang
